editorial:
You follow Frank, a laid-back boat repairman raising his brilliant niece Mary in a small Florida town. Mary is a math prodigy who can solve problems most adults cannot, but Frank just wants her to have a normal childhood with friends and recess. When Mary's grandmother Evelyn shows up and demands custody to push her into an elite academy, the family lands in a tense court battle that tests everyone's idea of what is best for a gifted kid. The movie has a warm, easygoing vibe with plenty of heart and humor, and the bond between Frank and Mary feels real from the first scene.

The acting is the standout here, especially the young lead who carries the film with charm and surprising depth. Chris Evans is relaxed and likable as Frank, and the supporting cast keeps things grounded. The pacing is smooth and never drags, though the courtroom scenes can feel a bit familiar. If you enjoy heartfelt family dramas with a smart kid at the center, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Frank and Evelyn reach a compromise instead of a winner-takes-all ruling. Mary stays living with Frank in Florida, but she also attends a gifted school part-time so her talent is nurtured. Evelyn gets regular visitation and a real role in Mary's life. Frank also keeps his teaching job and his relationship with Mary's teacher Bonnie. The story closes with Mary happily back home, showing that love and balance matter more than pushing a child to be extraordinary.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about gifted kids.
